title: Salad Dressings
description:
This is similar to what they serve at all the bistros in France. A simple salad with this tasty dressing is the perfect accompaniment to an omelet, a sandwich, or just bread and cheese.
You can mix into this snipped or chopped fresh chives, thyme, basil, marjoram, rosemary, or parsley.
This next version is more like what they call “French Dressing” in the U.S. However, it’s completely unlike the “orange horror available on the grocer’s shelf,” rather, it’s a “sweet-tart golden beauty of a dressing.”)
Salad Dressings – Some Basics
Pulse all the ingredients, except oil, in a food processor or blender until combined.
With the motor running, add oil in a slow stream and process until well combined.
Taste to see if you want any additional salt or pepper.
Chill, covered, until ready to use or up to 2 weeks.
ingredients: 1 cup of extra virgin olive oil
You can use this basic method to produce all the dressings here.
directions: And be sure to experiment with different ingredients, spices, or types and ratios of oil and vinegar. The classic mix is 2 parts oil to 1 part vinegar, but suit yourself – always!
This balsamic dressing is more deeply flavored than anything you’ll buy in a bottle.
In serving the salads, never drown them in dressing. Place some dressing in the base of the bowl with layers of greens, etc. on top. Toss at the table before serving.
1 cup of canola or olive oil
¼ cup white vinegar or lemon
